subject: BrightPath POC: evaluation gates, owners, and blocker register
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightpathhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: BrightPath POC: evaluation gates, owners, and blocker register

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion. Below is a concise recap of what we agreed for the 4-week evaluation (POC) and the concrete next steps. Please confirm or flag anything off before EOD Monday so we can lock the calendar and owners.

POC scope (high level)
- Integrate Redwood hosted inference to BrightPath ingestion pipeline for 3 representative workflows (clinical summarization, triage prompt, and patient message generation).
- Run parallel baseline (current heuristic) and compare quality, latency, and cost.

Success criteria (must pass at least 3/4 to move to business review)
1) Quality: automated evals + manual review — target F1/QA pass rate >= 88% on prioritized prompt set.
2) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end <= 420ms for the triage workflow under test load.
3) Cost: token-based unit cost <= $0.0035 per 1k tokens with recommended batching/quantization settings.
4) Safety/regulatory: no PII leakage incidents in sample review; SOC2 evidence for how inference logs are stored and retained.

Evaluation plan and timeline
- Week 0 (this week): install integration sandbox and share checklist. (Owner: Sean)
- Week 1: run functional tests, ingest sample data, and validate end-to-end. (Owners: BrightPath devs + Redwood engineering)
- Week 2: automated quality pass + manual spot checks. (Owners: BrightPath clinical SMEs + Monica)
- Week 3: load test and cost tuning; surface days-to-escrow metrics. (Owners: Sean + Dev)
- Week 4: executive review and go/no-go decision.

Ownership (point people)
- BrightPath: Alex Chen (technical lead), Priya Rao (program manager)
- Redwood: Sean Gallagher (eng-sponsor, timeline owner), Monica Patel (CS lead, quality owner), Dev Patel (eng triage/bug owner)

Blocker/escalation expectations
- If any blocking defect (production-affecting streaming, persistent 5xxs, or data-safety issue) arises, raise a Jira ticket with INF priority and CC Monica + Dev. Redwood will respond with triage within 4 hours and an ETA for mitigation or rollback.

Attachments: BrightPath_POC_checklist.xlsx (checklist + acceptance gates), SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf (redwood summary).

Next steps (action items)
- Alex/Priya: confirm agreement on success criteria, sign the MA (mutual action) and provide 3 sample doc sets by Monday EOD.
- Redwood: share sandbox creds and the checklist; schedule kick-off test session on Wed.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T17:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightPath POC: evaluation gates, owners, and blocker register

Thanks Sean — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A few small updates from our side: 

1) Quality criterion: can we add a manual reviewer pass specifically for clinical correctness on the triage prompts (we'll provide 50 gold cases)? If Redwood's manual review hits >= 90% clinical correctness we mark that criterion satisfied.
2) Latency target: 420ms 95p is acceptable, but we need a clear breakdown: network+processing. Can Redwood provide a per-hop timing breakdown in the Week 2 report?
3) SOC2: we'll need copies of the specific controls around logging and log retention (not just a summary) for our security review team.

On samples: we'll deliver the 3 sample doc sets (de-identified) by Monday EOD. Also scheduling: Wednesday kick-off at 10am PT works for our devs.

For blockers: noted — if anything blocks our test runs (esp. streaming disconnects), we'll open a ticket and reach out directly.

Alex
Alex Chen
Senior Engineering Manager, Integrations | BrightPath Health
alex.chen@brightpathhealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightpathhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightPath POC: evaluation gates, owners, and blocker register

Thanks Alex — confirmed on the manual clinical correctness gate. Sean: I attached an updated checklist with the reviewer plan and a column for "clinical reviewer score".

Quick notes on instrumentation (requested by Alex):
- We'll provide per-request timing: ingress, model infer, kv-cache lookup, egress time (CSV export) by Week 2.
- Security docs: SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf attached now; if BrightPath wants the control mappings we'll extract the logging control artifacts and share as a follow-up.

Mitigation playbook (if we encounter a streaming disconnect or high-5xx rate):
1) Immediate: failover to a short-window synchronous call (model variant) to keep latency bounded — this is a temporary fallback we can enable via routing policy.
2) Short-term: increase autoscale buffer + move load to Dedicated pool if we see headroom issues.
3) Long-term: Engineering patch for root cause. Escalation: file INF-XXXX in Jira and set priority P0/P1 depending on user impact.

I've assigned Dev as the engineering triage owner. Dev, please confirm you can pick up P0s within 4 hours (we agreed this on the call).

Attachment: BrightPath_POC_checklist.xlsx

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Priya Rao <priya@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightPath POC: evaluation gates, owners, and blocker register

Folks — jumping in with an initial test result from our Week 1 runs. We're seeing intermittent streaming disconnects when a single document pushes ~4k tokens (long patient notes). Sample error below: 

--- error snippet ---
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":{"message":"upstream connection reset during stream write","type":"server_error"}}
--- end snippet ---

Attached is a short error log extract (api_error_log_20261214.txt). This is blocking our end-to-end validation for the summarization workflow — once that reproduces reliably we can't complete quality checks.

Can you triage and advise next steps? If this will take more than a day to patch we need a temporary workaround so we can continue the other flows.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Rao
Program Manager | BrightPath Health
priya@brightpathhealth.com

Attachment: api_error_log_20261214.txt

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@brightpathhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightPath POC: evaluation gates, owners, and blocker register

Thanks Priya — I've created a Jira ticket (INF-4123) and attached the initial trace link. Short triage notes: 
- Initial hypothesis: streaming buffer regression when message frames exceed 4096 tokens combined with edge-case upstream connection resets on the managed gateway.
- Immediate mitigation: enable the routing fallback to the short-window synchronous call for the summarization workflow (this preserves correctness and gives deterministic latency). I can flip this on for your sandbox cluster now; it will appear as a config toggle in the console.
- ETA for hotfix (probable): 24-36 hours for a safe patch and rollout to hosted infra; we will run preflight tests in the canary region before broader rollout.

Escalation path: if the issue shows as "blocking for production validation" after mitigation, Monica will open a critical escalation with Engineering Leadership and we will commit to a 6-hour emergency window for rollback/patch.

Link to triage doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123
Link to temporary toggle: https://console.redwood.com/projects/bp-sandbox/routing

I'll enable the fallback now and notify when it's live.

--
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@brightpathhealth.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightPath POC: evaluation gates, owners, and blocker register

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary of agreed next steps: 
- Dev: enable routing fallback for summarization in BP sandbox now (Dev to confirm when toggled).
- BrightPath: validate end-to-end once fallback is enabled and report any remaining regressions (Priya).
- Redwood: aim to ship hotfix in 24-36 hours and publish preflight results to the triage doc.
- Monica: if BrightPath still can't proceed after fallback, open escalation and we'll commit to 6-hour emergency window.

I've scheduled a 30-minute sync for Thursday 10:00am PT to review progress and share preflight numbers — calendar invite sent.

Action reminders: please upload your 3 sample de-identified doc sets into the Drive folder and confirm SOC2 control artifact request (Alex).

Looking forward to the kick-off validation.

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
